description: A chat conversation component with message rendering, typing indicators, attachments, and send input.

parameters.name: CurrentUser
parameters.description: The currently authenticated user.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes.

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Whether the input is disabled.

parameters.name: Messages
parameters.description: List of messages to display.

parameters.name: OnSendMessage
parameters.description: Fired when the user sends a message (text only). Retained for backward compatibility.

parameters.name: OnSend
parameters.description: Fired when the user sends a message, carrying optional thread/reply context.

parameters.name: OnAttachmentClick
parameters.description: Fired when an attachment is clicked.

parameters.name: Placeholder
parameters.description: Placeholder for the message input.

parameters.name: TypingUsers
parameters.description: Users currently typing.

parameters.name: TypingLabel
parameters.description: Replaces the localized typing text with a host-computed label. The built-in text comes from the TmChat_TypingSingle/TmChat_TypingTwo/TmChat_TypingMany resources ("{0} is typing…"); a set label receives the current TypingUsers list and its result is rendered instead — e.g. users => $"{users[0].Name} píše…". Null (the default) keeps the localized text. TypingTemplate takes precedence: the template replaces the WHOLE indicator, the label only its text span.

parameters.name: TypingTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the WHOLE built-in typing indicator with host markup. The template receives the current TypingUsers list; the built-in .tm-chat__typing-indicator element (dots + text) is not rendered at all. Null (the default) renders the built-in indicator. Markup passed into the template carries the HOST's CSS scope, not TmChat.razor.css. The TypingTimeout expiry applies to the template TOO: an expired window renders NEITHER the built-in indicator NOR the template (the next TypingUsers change reopens the window). TypingAriaHidden by contrast applies ONLY to the built-in indicator — a template sets its own AT visibility. Do NOT put aria-live or role="status" into the template: TmChat keeps one live region of its own and typing is never announced by the component, so an extra live region inside the template would only risk double announcements.

parameters.name: TypingAriaHidden
parameters.description: Hides the WHOLE built-in typing indicator from assistive technology by rendering aria-hidden="true" on its wrapper — not just the decorative dots, which always carry their own aria-hidden. Default false (today's markup: the wrapper has no aria-hidden and its text stays reachable). For a host that conveys typing through its own live region, set this to true so the indicator is not double-read; typing itself is NEVER announced by the component.

parameters.name: TypingTimeout
parameters.description: Auto-hides the typing indicator when the host stops sending fresh TypingUsers. The expiry applies to BOTH the built-in indicator and a TypingTemplate — an expired window renders neither. The expiry window is measured from the LAST CHANGE of TypingUsers: a new list instance OR a different content (order-sensitive, per-ChatUser value equality) opens a fresh window, an identical list reference with unchanged content does not — pass a stable reference and re-assign the list only on real typing signals, or every parent re-render extends the window forever. When the window expires the indicator disappears but the host's TypingUsers list is never mutated; the next change reopens it. Null (the default) never expires. A non-positive timeout (TimeSpan.Zero or negative) expires IMMEDIATELY: the indicator is suppressed from the next render and no timer is armed. The clock is the injected TimeProvider (fallback TimeProvider.System), so tests drive expiry with a FakeTimeProvider. A set timeout arms a single-shot timer that is cancelled in DisposeAsync — no dangling timer after unmount.

parameters.name: OnEditMessage
parameters.description: Fired when the user commits an edit to one of their messages.

parameters.name: OnDeleteMessage
parameters.description: Fired when the user deletes one of their messages.

parameters.name: OnToggleReaction
parameters.description: Fired when the user toggles an emoji reaction on a message.

parameters.name: OnReply
parameters.description: Fired when the user opens a message's reply thread.

parameters.name: OnMessageRead
parameters.description: Fired once per incoming message when it first becomes visible, for read receipts.

parameters.name: ActiveThreadRootId
parameters.description: Id of the thread root whose reply panel is open. Two-way bindable.

parameters.name: ActiveThreadRootIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the open thread changes.

parameters.name: EnableThreads
parameters.description: When true, replies are grouped into a thread panel instead of shown inline. Default true.

parameters.name: EnableReactions
parameters.description: When true, messages show a reaction bar and emoji picker. Default true.

parameters.name: AllowEditDelete
parameters.description: When true, the current user can edit and delete their own messages. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowReadReceipts
parameters.description: When true, own messages display per-user read receipts. Default true.

parameters.name: AutoReadReceipts
parameters.description: When true, incoming messages fire OnMessageRead as they render. Default true.

parameters.name: ReactionEmojis
parameters.description: Emoji offered by the reaction picker.

parameters.name: MessageTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in message row with host markup for the messages selected by UseTemplateFor. The template receives a ChatMessageContext per rendered message: Message, IsOwn, InThread, Index, IsFirstInGroup, a typed payload accessor (context.PayloadAs<T>()), a metadata accessor (context.GetMetadata<T>(key, fallback)) and DefaultContent — the built-in row, so ordinary messages can fall back to the default look. Precedence: when null, every message renders the built-in row (today's behavior). When set and UseTemplateFor is null, the template renders for EVERY message (including thread panel messages). When both are set, the template renders only for messages where UseTemplateFor returns true — the host thus overrides just its "special" kinds (e.g. m => m.Kind == "ai-draft"). Regardless of the template, TmChat still owns everything around the message: each message keeps a wrapper element with data-message-id (and data-kind when the message carries a Kind) used for scroll anchoring and read receipts; the thread filter, draft guard and read-receipt reporting are unaffected. Note that markup passed into the template carries the HOST's CSS scope — the TmChat.razor.css scoped classes do not apply to it.

parameters.name: UseTemplateFor
parameters.description: Restricts MessageTemplate to the messages for which the predicate returns true. Null (the default) means the template renders for every message. Typical host usage: m => m.Kind == "ai-draft" to override only special kinds while ordinary messages keep the built-in row.

parameters.name: OnDraftChanged
parameters.description: Fires whenever the TmChatDraftState value changes — a composer or thread-reply slot gained/lost text, or a message edit opened/changed/closed. Value-equality deduped, so it does NOT fire on every keystroke. The composer, the thread panel's reply input and the inline message edit hold text the host cannot observe through any parameter; use TmChatDraftState to build a dirty-guard before a reload or navigation that would silently discard an in-progress message. Opening an edit reports EditingMessageId immediately while HasUnsavedContent stays false until the text differs from the message as it was when the edit started.

parameters.name: ComposerTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in composer (the input textarea + send button) with host markup — a subscribe gate, a PPV field, an owner note + hint, anything the consumer domain needs. The template receives a live ChatComposerContext: bind the host input to Text (the source of truth), push each keystroke with SetTextAsync and send with SendAsync so the draft guard (HasUnsavedDraft, OnDraftChanged) and the send path (OnSendMessage / OnSend, submit state) keep working exactly as for the built-in composer; mirror CanSend on a custom send button. When set, the built-in composer does NOT render (.tm-chat__input and .tm-chat__send-btn disappear from the DOM) and neither ComposerAddon nor ComposerFooter render — the template owns the whole composer area, and markup passed into the template carries the HOST's CSS scope, not TmChat.razor.css. The .tm-chat__input-area wrapper itself STAYS (its padding and border-top), carrying tm-chat__input-area--custom so the template's markup stacks vertically instead of the textarea + send flex row. Ignored when ShowComposer is false.

parameters.name: ComposerAddon
parameters.description: Content rendered ABOVE the built-in composer input, inside the composer area — an owner note, a hint or a short status line. Only rendered with the built-in composer (a ComposerTemplate replaces the whole area and renders its own chrome).

parameters.name: ComposerFooter
parameters.description: Content rendered BELOW the built-in composer input row — a footnote, a remaining-character count or a secondary action. Only rendered with the built-in composer (a ComposerTemplate replaces the whole area and renders its own chrome).

parameters.name: ComposerDescribedBy
parameters.description: Ids of host elements, e.g. inside ComposerAddon/ComposerFooter, describing the composer input. Rendered as aria-describedby on the built-in textarea; omitted from the DOM while null (the default). With a ComposerTemplate the built-in textarea does not render — describe the host-owned input there instead.

parameters.name: ShowComposer
parameters.description: Whether the composer renders at all. false drops the composer area from the DOM — the read-only / viewing variant of a chat. Default true (today's behavior). When false, ComposerTemplate is ignored too. Note this covers only the MAIN composer: the thread panel's reply input is separate — a truly read-only chat also needs EnableThreads=false and AllowEditDelete=false so no reply input, edit or delete affordance renders.

parameters.name: BannerContent
parameters.description: Content rendered ABOVE the message list — a connection banner (offline / reconnecting) or any conversation-level callout. Rendered raw: TmChat adds NO wrapper element and deliberately does NOT turn the banner into an aria-live region. TmChat may own exactly one live region; if the banner content should be announced, put the role="status" (or an explicit aria-live) on an element INSIDE this slot with short, host-controlled text.

parameters.name: HeaderContent
parameters.description: Content rendered at the VERY TOP of the component, above BannerContent and the message list — a conversation title bar or header controls. Rendered raw (no wrapper), so the host markup owns its layout. Note that an OPEN THREAD PANEL OVERLAYS it: the thread panel is absolutely positioned over the component (top/right/bottom), so while a thread is open the panel covers the header area on the panel's side.

parameters.name: EmptyContent
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in empty state (the icon + "no messages" texts) when the conversation has no messages. The built-in empty state is fully dropped, so the host owns the empty-scenario copy. The content renders RAW at the top of the message list (no wrapper element); the built-in look fills the list and centers its content, so the host's slot root should use flex:1 plus vertical/horizontal centering. Only applies while Messages is empty; with messages present the slot is not rendered.

parameters.name: EnterToSend
parameters.description: Whether pressing Enter in a composer input submits. Default true (today's behavior: the built-in composer, the thread panel's reply input and an open message edit all submit on Enter). false makes Enter a NATIVE new line in all three inputs — nothing is sent from Enter itself, only from the send button, SendAsync or Ctrl/⌘+Enter (no Shift/Alt, outside an IME composition; handled by chat.js). Shift+Enter always inserts a new line and Alt/Ctrl/Meta+Enter always stay native (browser and host shortcuts). The keydown handling lives in the chat.js module once it is attached (it also owns the IME guard, which a net8 KeyboardEventArgs cannot express); this parameter is passed to the module as its enterToSend option and re-attaches the module when it changes.

parameters.name: RefocusAfterSend
parameters.description: Whether the composer input is focused again after a SUCCESSFUL send. Default true — after the send handlers complete and the composer clears, focus returns to the input (the built-in textarea, or the element a custom composer registered through AttachAsync) so the user can type the next message without reaching for the mouse. Set false for hosts that move focus themselves (e.g. into a confirmation UI). A failed send (a handler that throws) does not refocus — the text is preserved and the user keeps their context.

parameters.name: ShowAvatars
parameters.description: Whether the built-in message rows show the author avatar. Default true (today's behavior); set false for consumers whose bubbles carry no avatars. The switch applies to the built-in rows only — a MessageTemplate renders its own markup and decides about avatars itself.

parameters.name: AutoScroll
parameters.description: When the component scrolls the message list to the bottom on its own. Default WhenAtBottom — the ONLY documented change of TmChat's default behavior (scrolling used to be a no-op): the first render lands at the bottom and further messages scroll only while the user is at the bottom; messages arriving above the reading position are counted behind the jump-to-new button, the user's own messages always scroll and a prepend of older history preserves the visual position. Never restores the pre-2.10 behavior — the component itself makes no scroll calls at all (the explicit ScrollToBottomAsync / ScrollToMessageAsync helpers still work, the jump-to-new button does not render); Always pins the list to the bottom on every message change regardless of the reading position.

parameters.name: OnLoadOlder
parameters.description: Fired when the user reaches the top edge of the message list (through the built-in "load older" affordance or the scroller's near-top report) and older history should be PREPENDED to Messages. The host loads the page and updates the parameter — the component detects the prepend (the first message Id changed, the last stayed) and preserves the visual position instead of scrolling. Only consulted when HasMoreBefore is true and while IsLoadingOlder is false. Not wired → neither the built-in affordance nor the top-edge trigger render (additive — hosts without pagination keep today's DOM).

parameters.name: HasMoreBefore
parameters.description: Whether older history exists above the current page (the host's "has more" cursor). Together with a wired OnLoadOlder it renders the built-in "load older" affordance at the top of the message list and arms the top-edge trigger. Default false (no pagination — today's DOM).

parameters.name: IsLoadingOlder
parameters.description: Whether the host is currently loading the older page (its own loading state, mirrored into the component). While true the "load older" affordance is disabled and neither it nor the top-edge trigger fires OnLoadOlder again. Default false.

parameters.name: ShowJumpToNewButton
parameters.description: Whether the floating jump-to-new button renders when messages arrive while the user is reading above the bottom. Default true. The button shows the count of the unseen messages (TmChat_NewMessages plural family; replaced by JumpToNewTemplate) and scrolling back to the bottom — by the user or through the button — resets it. Never renders with AutoScroll=ChatAutoScroll.Never.

parameters.name: JumpToNewTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the CONTENT of the floating jump-to-new button (icon + localized count) with host markup. The template receives the current count of unseen messages; the <button> element itself stays built-in (its click — scroll to the bottom, count reset, composer refocus — and the TmChat_JumpToNew aria-label are the component's). Null (the default) renders the built-in content.

parameters.name: MessageAnnouncement
parameters.description: The text announced for ONE new message, supplied by the host (localized, with its domain context). The component never invents sentences. A null func or a null/whitespace result means 'do not announce this message' — the default state is a silent chat. Only messages APPENDED to the end of the rendered root list are candidates: the initial load, a fill from an empty list and a PREPEND of older history are not announced, thread replies render in the thread panel (announce them through AnnounceAsync) and the user's own messages are skipped unless AnnounceOwnMessages is true. Announcements share the AnnouncementThrottle trailing window with AnnounceAsync — a burst within the window is summarized by BatchAnnouncement or collapsed to the LATEST text.

parameters.name: BatchAnnouncement
parameters.description: Optional summary for a burst announced TOGETHER: when at least TWO messages wait in one AnnouncementThrottle window (a host action mixed into the window is composed around the summary, never summarized away), the trailing flush announces this instead of the last individual text (e.g. batch => $"{batch.Count} new messages"). The delegate receives the messages held by the window. A null result falls back to the last individual text; a single held message is announced through its own text without consulting the summary.

parameters.name: AnnouncementThrottle
parameters.description: The trailing throttle window shared by the message pipeline and AnnounceAsync. Default 1 second. Within the window the latest announcement wins and is flushed when the window ends; a free window flushes immediately (the first message of a quiet conversation is never delayed). A non-positive value disables throttling — every announcement flushes immediately. The clock is the injected TimeProvider (fallback TimeProvider.System), so tests drive the window with a FakeTimeProvider; the pending timer is cancelled in DisposeAsync.

parameters.name: AnnounceOwnMessages
parameters.description: Whether the current user's own messages are announced. Default false — the user knows what they typed. 'Own' matches the built-in bubble logic: an Outgoing message or one authored by CurrentUser. System messages are not own and are announced like any other when MessageAnnouncement produces text for them.

parameters.name: MessagesAriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the messages container (a scrollable role=region with tabindex=0). Default: the localized TmChat_MessagesLabel. The container is deliberately NOT a role=log — log implies aria-live and would make a second live region out of it; new messages are announced through the component's own region instead. A page with SEVERAL chats should pass a DISTINCT label per chat — the container is a named landmark and a Tab stop, so two chats labelled 'Messages' are indistinguishable in the landmark list.

parameters.name: ComposerAriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the built-in composer textarea. Default: the effective placeholder (the host's Placeholder or the localized TmChat_Placeholder) — until this parameter existed the textarea had only a placeholder, which is no accessible name. Ignored with a ComposerTemplate (the template owns its own input).
